_doc: Pass criteria of the core regression suite. Each block names the earlier result it is taken from (file and line, run directory) and why each tolerance has its size. Read by the judge scripts; change only with a JOURNAL.md entry.

G.published_source: refs/arxiv_2611.12831/src/main.tex lines 824-833 (dt = 0.01 M to t = 230 M)
G.rel_tol_vs_earlier_why: earlier errors are quoted to four digits in docs/TESTLOG.md; a change of the pusher, the metric or the Hermite lattice changes them by far more
G.r_peri_abs_tol_why: docs/TESTLOG.md line 20 quotes r_p to six decimals
G.rel_tol_vs_published_why: two significant digits in the paper (rounding allows up to 4 percent: 1.254e-7 against 1.3e-7)
G.order_why: pairwise orders of the final position error between dt = 0.005, 0.01, 0.02 M were 1.9989 to 2.0003 (kerr_summary.json C.dt_convergence_ks); the table entry tab:outcomes says 1.995-2.001 (fit over five steps)
G.traj_abs_tol_why: largest earlier processor-against-card difference of the same run, 1.8e-8 in position (kerr_summary.json D, bchol_lat_dt0.01): anything below is round-off ordering, not a change of the method

O.earlier: runs/os/nocap_sc (docs/TESTLOG.md lines 860-880; paper/sections/tables/tab_outcomes.tex table tab:outcomes_dust rows 'first apparent horizon' and 'M_AH/M at formation')
O.t_first_ah_abs_tol_why: one search interval of the finder (16 cycles of dt = 9.46e-3 M = 0.151 M)
O.m_abs_tol_vs_earlier_why: successive searches of the earlier run scatter between 0.9997 and 1.0005 from formation to 22 M
O.alpha_abs_tol_before_ah_why: the two deposition rules (finest level, adaptive level) differ by up to 4e-3 in the central lapse (docs/TESTLOG.md line 726); a change of that kind must show
O.max_H_rel_tol_why: largest Hamiltonian-constraint norm 1.90 at 17.3 M (table tab:outcomes_dust); the adaptive cloud level gives 4.7

F.factor_why: the errors are those of fourth-order Runge-Kutta at a quarter-cell step on ordinary differential equations; a change of the step or of the source conversion changes them by orders of magnitude, round-off by far less than a factor two
F.tau_probe_max_why: twice the largest earlier relative error of the probe proper time (4.0e-5 over the run; 1.7e-5 at t = 2, cosmo/TESTLOG.md line 69); the code has since made it third order (cosmo/TESTLOG.md line 127)
F.tau_probe_end_max_why: set on 2026-11-15 03:50 after the first regression run (JOURNAL.md): the probe proper time is third order since 95b5c47 (cosmo/TESTLOG.md line 127); the earlier second-order run ends at 1.7e-5, the regression run core-20261115-032615-45e1779 at 1.0e-7; a return to second order fails this check

L.linear_rel_tol_why: earlier: within 0.5 percent of linear theory at both probes up to a_p = 30 (cosmo/TESTLOG.md line 166); measured again from the earlier run: 0.45 and 0.31 percent
L.earlier_rel_tol_why: the earlier run differs from this one only by processor against card and by later code changes on paths these options do not use; 1e-3 of the contrast is ten times below the agreement with linear theory
L.variant_why: the earlier run used the relativistic ('number') displacement, then the default of cosmo/ic/make_east.py (its id.json: displacement_factor 4.0396); growth/run.py passes --displacement number
